name: Tecuamburro
status: Natural-state model, UQ & resource assessment complete
summary: High-enthalpy volcanic system southeast of Guatemala City. One exploratory well reached 806m depth in andesitic lavas and pyroclastics at 235°C; geothermometry suggests the reservoir itself may reach up to 300°C. Now carried well beyond that single data point through our own natural-state calibration, full ensemble uncertainty quantification and automated resource assessment.
detail: Built from a single exploratory well and surface geoscience, our natural-state model was pushed through a full uncertainty-quantification ensemble rather than left as one best-fit realisation — the two cross-sections below show the resulting P10–P90 spread on the 250°C, 270°C and 290°C isotherms at Tecuamburro, and the equivalent 160–200°C bands at the neighbouring Infiernitos resource, both studied together as one combined system. An automated resource-assessment algorithm then sited production and injection wells directly against that ensemble, shown here for one representative sample run. This is the same methodology behind our Tecuamburro–Infiernitos manuscript currently in preparation, and the source of the calibrated permeability cross-sections shown on our Technology page.
